about.headline: Company with over 9 years of experience by your side in 5 countries
about.descriptionText: UZ GROW is a company operating in the field of modern greenhouse construction and agro-engineering. Our goal is to develop highly efficient, innovative and export-oriented greenhouse infrastructure in Uzbekistan.
about.missionDesc: Increasing customer income through the implementation of sustainable and profitable greenhouse projects that meet local and international standards.
about.visionDesc: To become a leading agro-engineering company in Central Asia and export modern greenhouses.

valuesAndRules.desc: Our values are the foundation of our work, our culture and our future direction.

about.businessScopeDesc: UZ-GROW is a professional company specialized in implementing modern greenhouse solutions and agrotechnologies. We are engaged in the construction of multi-span film greenhouses, solar greenhouses, planting and seedling greenhouses, livestock greenhouses, hydroponics systems, and smart greenhouses with automated control. We also provide comprehensive services for the preparation of greenhouse accessories, implementation of greenhouse projects of varying complexity, and introduction of modern water-saving irrigation systems.
about.professionalTeamDesc: The UZ-GROW team consists of professional designers, experienced technical engineers, and qualified mounting specialists. We lead all processes from design to installation and full commissioning under strict control. Every detail is ensured to meet high quality standards, providing our clients with reliable and long-term results.
about.descriptionTop: We are not an ordinary agricultural company — we are a team specialized in greenhouse engineering, modern constructions, and creating high-efficiency agro systems. Our technologies are adapted to various client needs, whether it’s a smart greenhouse or a traditional solar greenhouse — we offer the most optimal solution for every project. In particular, our experience in designing multi-span greenhouses allows for the most efficient use of land area.
about.descriptionBottom: Our main goal is to develop our customers’ business by providing high-quality, efficient, and economically beneficial agro solutions. We create systems that serve to increase yields, reduce costs, and ensure stable income. By choosing us, you select not a simple service, but a professional team that approaches its work responsibly. We are ready for long-term cooperation with you, successful implementation of your projects, and creating a bright future together. Wherever you are, we can offer the most suitable greenhouse solution. Let’s move towards success together!

Establishing and maintaining contact with customers
Designing and implementing projects
Fulfilling contractual and legal obligations
Controlling the quality of our services

sections.title: 3. Disclosure and Sharing of Data

items.name: Tomatoes
items.tagline: The most widely grown greenhouse crop with steady demand
items.intro: Greenhouse tomatoes crop over a long season and market demand for them is stable. High yields need plenty of light, even temperatures and moderate humidity. With automated climate control, drip irrigation and fertigation, a modern greenhouse yields several times more than open fields.
items.greenhouse: A tall (4–6 m), wide-span greenhouse: plants on a trellis grow to 3–4 m. Polycarbonate or multi-layer film, roof and side ventilation, winter heating and a thermal screen are recommended.
methods: On substrate (coco or rockwool) with drip irrigation and fertigation
In soil — a lower-cost start for small and medium farms
Vertical trellis growing — more yield per square metre

faq.q: Which greenhouse type is best for tomatoes?
faq.a: Commercial growing needs a tall, wide-span, well-ventilated greenhouse. A tunnel works on a small plot, but yield and season are shorter. We choose the exact type based on the local climate and area.

faq.q: Soil or substrate — which is better?
faq.a: Substrate (coco, rockwool) raises yield and quality and lowers disease risk, but costs more to start. Soil is cheaper to begin with. Many clients start in soil and move to substrate later.
In Uzbekistan’s climate, winter tomatoes need heating — night temperatures should not drop below 14–16 °C. The heating type (gas, coal, heat pump) is calculated in the project.

Yield depends on the variety, technology and greenhouse type; in a modern greenhouse it is several times higher than in open fields. We calculate exact figures for your region and method in the project.
Natural pollination is limited indoors, so bumblebee hives or special vibrators are used. This noticeably improves fruit set and quality.
It depends on the area, greenhouse type and equipment. We provide an exact schedule once the project is approved.

items.name: Cucumbers
items.tagline: Fast to mature, several harvests per season
items.intro: Greenhouse cucumbers grow fast and start fruiting about six weeks after transplanting. Two or three cycles a year are possible, which keeps income steady. Cucumbers love warmth and moisture, so an even climate is essential.
items.greenhouse: A greenhouse that holds humidity yet ventilates well. 3.5–5 m height for trellising, a fogging system and even heating are recommended. Polycarbonate retains heat better in winter.
methods: On substrate with automatic drip irrigation and fertigation
In soil with mulching and drip irrigation

faq.a: One that keeps a warm, humid climate but ventilates well. A tunnel for small plots, a tall multi-span greenhouse for commercial growing.
A heated greenhouse typically allows 2–3 cycles a year. Unheated greenhouses have a shorter season — spring and autumn.
Greenhouses mostly use parthenocarpic varieties, which set fruit without pollination.

faq.q: What if humidity is too high?
faq.a: Excess humidity causes fungal diseases, so ventilation and automatic humidity control matter.

faq.q: Can cucumbers and tomatoes share a greenhouse?
faq.a: Not recommended: cucumbers need warmer, more humid air, tomatoes drier air. Separate sections or greenhouses give better results.

faq.q: What area should I start with?
faq.a: A small farm can start with 0.1–0.2 ha. Commercially, 0.5 ha and above is usually more profitable. We calculate the details in the project.

items.name: Strawberries
items.tagline: A premium product grown on multi-tier shelving
items.intro: Greenhouse strawberries in winter and early spring are among the most expensive products on the market. Shelving or hanging gutters fit more plants per square metre, make picking easier and keep berries clean. Cool nights are important for flowering, so climate control is the key factor.
items.greenhouse: A greenhouse with shelving or hanging gutters: plants at 1–1.5 m height for easy care and picking. Good ventilation, night temperature control and supplementary lighting where needed are recommended.
methods: On shelving or hanging gutters on substrate (most common)
Vertical multi-tier system — many plants on a small area

faq.q: Why grow strawberries on shelving instead of soil?
faq.a: Berries don’t touch the ground, so they are cleaner and less prone to disease, and picking is faster. More plants fit per square metre.
Depending on the plants, 2–3 months after planting. Day-neutral varieties fruit over a long period in a greenhouse.

faq.q: Can they be grown in winter?
faq.a: Yes, a heated greenhouse with supplementary lighting can produce in winter — exactly when prices are highest.
Bee or bumblebee hives are placed in the greenhouse. Good pollination gives large, well-shaped berries.
It depends on the region, season and sales goal. Our specialists advise on suitable varieties during the project stage.

faq.q: Can I start on a small area?
faq.a: Yes. Vertical shelving lets you fit many plants even on a small area.

items.name: Greens and lettuce
items.tagline: Short cycle, 8–10 harvests a year — ideal for hydroponics
items.intro: Lettuce, basil, dill, parsley and other greens are ready in 4–6 weeks. Hydroponically they grow without soil, clean and uniform, and a greenhouse lets you grow them all year. A steady product for restaurants, supermarkets and export.
items.greenhouse: A greenhouse fitted with hydroponic gutters (NFT) or floating rafts (DWC). A shade screen and cooling against overheating, and light heating in winter, are recommended.
methods: NFT — gutters with a thin film of nutrient solution

faq.q: What is hydroponics and why does it suit greens?
faq.a: In hydroponics plants grow without soil, in a nutrient solution. Greens have small roots and short cycles, so the method is the most efficient for them: less water, cleaner produce.
With a 30–45 day cycle, a greenhouse can produce 8–10 harvests a year.

faq.q: How much water does it use?
faq.a: Water recirculates and is reused, so consumption is far lower than in open fields.
Various lettuces, basil, dill, parsley, coriander, spinach, rocket and more.
The nutrient solution is controlled automatically. After installation we train your staff to run the system.
Restaurants, cafés, supermarkets and wholesale markets — demand for clean, consistent greens exists all year.

items.name: Seedling production
items.tagline: Healthy seedlings are half of a good harvest
items.intro: Seedlings of tomatoes, cucumbers, peppers, cabbage and other crops are grown in trays in a dedicated nursery greenhouse. Even temperature, humidity and light make them healthy and uniform. A nursery is a source of income both for your own farm and for sale.
items.greenhouse: A greenhouse with benches, fogging and precise temperature control. A shade screen and supplementary lighting for even light, and heating in winter.
methods: In trays with peat or substrate mix

faq.q: Why grow seedlings in a separate greenhouse?
faq.a: Seedlings need a different climate from the main crop — warmer and more humid. In a separate nursery they are healthier and more uniform, with lower disease risk.

faq.q: How much area does a nursery need?
faq.a: Because seedlings grow in trays, a nursery is much smaller than the main greenhouse. Its size is calculated from the number of seedlings you need.

faq.q: Can I grow seedlings for sale?
faq.a: Yes, demand for healthy seedlings is high in spring — a separate income stream.
A productive variety is grafted onto a hardy rootstock with strong roots. Such seedlings resist soil diseases better and yield more.
Benches, trays, a fogging or ebb-and-flow system, temperature and humidity control, and supplementary lighting if needed.

faq.q: Can seedlings be grown in winter?
faq.a: Yes, with heating and lighting, seedlings are prepared in late winter for spring planting.
